raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Quark's MXFP8 path drops `activation_quant_key`, so a weight-only checkpoint can select a backend that quantizes activations to FP8. This fix passes the key through kernel selection: weight-only requests select Marlin or emulation, preserving unquantized activations. Fixes #65193.

## Claims

- Explicit weight-only requests skip W8A8 kernels; forcing an incompatible backend fails during selection.
- Callers that omit the activation key retain existing W8A8 selection and A16 fallback behavior.
- Regression coverage includes real Quark layer construction and checkpoint loading through `LLM.generate`.

## Validation

Tested patch: `392d905e03`; base: `e8570ef757`. One physical H200 NVL, Torch `2.14.0+cu132`, with precompiled vLLM binaries pinned to the base.

| Check | Red 1: base | Green: patch | Red 2: fix removed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MXFP8 + MXFP4 selection | 11 failed, 64 passed | 75 passed | 11 failed, 64 passed |
| Real Quark checkpoint + LLM | 1 failed: backend assertion | 1 passed | 1 failed: backend assertion |

All three stages used identical tests and binaries; only five production Python files changed. On H200, both red runs selected Humming and failed the weight-only backend assertion; green selected Marlin and generated two tokens.

[Full logs, exit codes, source hashes and replay scripts](https://gist.github.com/anhtud/1fffb3879b97711ea8b50245f8c3b588).

Additional checks passed: three Quark-to-Marlin GEMM shapes against a BF16-activation reference, pre-commit hooks (including Ruff, mypy and test tethering), and `git diff --check`. The Buildkite quantization job includes the new E2E regression.

**Remaining validation:** physical Blackwell execution and trained-model accuracy/perplexity evaluation. SM100/103/120/121 selection uses simulated hardware capability. The synthetic checkpoint validates dispatch and generation, not trained-model accuracy. No throughput benchmark was run.

**Draft status:** human line-by-line review and representative model evaluation remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands, checkpoint setup and output</summary>

Full revisions:
- Base: `e8570ef757b67805797b005b59fcd6600d939421`
- Tested patch: `392d905e035015e673ecd033b54f5bbee87bed34`

Run from the source checkout using the isolated environment's Python:

```bash
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp8_kernel_selection.py \
  tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py -q
/work/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/quantization/test_mxfp8.py::test_quark_mxfp8_weight_only_checkpoint -v -s
```

The E2E test creates a seeded tiny Llama safetensors checkpoint with Quark weight-only MXFP8 metadata, loads real weights through `LLM`, checks the selected kernels, and generates two tokens. Setup and replay scripts are included with the logs.

Condensed output:

```text
red1 / red2, Quark SM100 selection:
assert isinstance(scheme.ocp_mx_linear, expected)
E assert False
E ... FlashInferCutedslMxfp8LinearKernel ... MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel
11 failed, 64 passed

red1 / red2, real H200 checkpoint:
Using HummingMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
Exception: Call to collective_rpc method failed: assert False
... check_kernels ...
1 failed, 6 warnings

green, selection:
75 passed

green, real H200 checkpoint:
Using MarlinMxfp8LinearKernel for MXFP8 GEMM
1 passed, 6 warnings
```

Both suites returned exit code `1 → 0 → 1`. Source hashes confirm identical tests across stages and that the green source matches the tested commit.

The numerical check used `(M,N,K) = (1,128,128), (17,256,256), (3,130,256)`. Observed maximum absolute error was `0.0` for all three shapes; assertion tolerances were `rtol=0.02`, `atol=0.02`.

</details>

## Details

- **Compatibility:** the selector/config default is `kMxfp8Dynamic`; explicit `None` requests weight-only execution. Selection reuses the existing activation override resolution and adds a `_supports_quant_scheme` gate.
- **Backend support:** `input_quant_key()` describes external input/fusion support and does not identify internal activation precision. Marlin and emulation explicitly accept weight-only requests and retain the existing A16 fallback for W8A8. Other MXFP8 implementations default to requiring dynamic MXFP8 activations. The gate adds no inference hot-path work or synchronization; backend performance can differ and was not benchmarked.
- **Related work:** the pre-submission duplicate check found no open PR directly fixing #65193. #63378 covers MoE and leaves dense MXFP8 for follow-up; #59460 covers fallback reporting/enforcement and identifies this missing key as a gap. Reconciliation may be needed if #59460 lands first. The issue author had announced a staged implementation, but no matching open PR was found at submission.

AI assistance was used to implement the change, run validation and prepare this PR.

+## MXFP8 weight-only linear layers
+
+For Quark OCP-MX MXFP8 checkpoints without input activation quantization,

+checkpoint's activation format.
